about: Numbers the elections calendar and law code use, each tagged SOURCED, ESTIMATED (with its source and spread) or TUNABLE (with the spread it's checked against). Read by src/core2/elections-calendar.ts and src/core2/election-ties.ts.

votersPerVotingLocation.source: Active registered voters per voting location in the November 2022 general election: 203,660,564 active registered voters over 94,793 voting locations (U.S. Election Assistance Commission, 2022 Election Administration and Voting Survey Data Brief, United States). Sizes how many precincts' polling places a town has.

pollWorkersPerVotingLocation.source: Poll workers per voting location in the November 2022 general election: 645,219 poll workers over 94,793 voting locations (U.S. Election Assistance Commission, 2022 Election Administration and Voting Survey Data Brief, United States).

specialElectionDaysEstimate.source: Days from a vacancy to the special election where the state's law row is not read (special-election-law.json). The earlier engine used three months everywhere; state laws run from about 60 days (a governor's call with a short notice) to the next general election (NCSL, Filling Legislative Vacancies; Ballotpedia, How vacancies are filled in state legislatures).

restoredFractionOfDisenfranchised.source: The Sentencing Project, Locked Out 2022 and 2024: about half of those disenfranchised have finished their sentences, the share a law restoring the vote after a sentence returns (0.5 of 1.7% of the voting-age population, nationally).

ballotFirstPositionShare.source: The vote share the first-listed candidate gains over a place further down the same ballot, read by every voter as a cue on the printed ballot; it decides only where nothing else separates the candidates. Koppell and Steen 2004, 'The Effects of Ballot Position on Election Outcomes', Journal of Politics 66(1):267-281: in New York City's 1998 Democratic primaries, with names rotated by precinct, first-listed candidates did better in 71 of 79 contests; Pasek, Schneider, Krosnick and others 2014, Public Opinion Quarterly 78(2):416-439, find smaller edges in California general elections. Two points is in the range both report.

exitPollBase.source: A voter's reluctance to stop for an exit pollster's questionnaire before their engagement, interest and temperament: set so about 45% of the voters approached tell, the response rate Edison Research gives (Pew Research Center, 'Just how does the general election exit poll work, anyway?', November 2, 2016: "about 45% of the voters the firm approaches agree to fill out questionnaires"; earlier "more like 60%"). Fitted on the named voters of three drawn race towns (src/core2/trait-test-kit.ts drawnRaceWorld, 30 days to two days past the race, every module): Finklea, South Carolina (place key 4525405, seed 100a9eddd8c1, 586 voters with a choice), Silver City, Nevada (3266800, 62fd4b12c74d, 122) and Douglas, Nebraska (3113505, d6f5f50c5452, 209): 46.5% pooled, 34% to 52% by town.

exitPollEngagementWeight.source: How much more readily a voter who follows politics closely tells the pollster, per unit of engagement (0 to 1) above the nation's average. Politically engaged adults are over-represented among survey respondents (Pew Research Center, 'What Low Response Rates Mean for Telephone Surveys', May 15, 2017: "politically engaged adults are overrepresented in surveys"; telephone polls overstate the registered share by about 7 points). No study gives the size against interest in the race, so engagement and interest are weighted equally per standard deviation among the voters (engagement 0.071, interest 0.903 in the fitting towns); only the ratio of the case to the trait weight is fitted.

exitPollInterestWeight.source: How much more readily a voter tells the pollster the more the day's races mattered to them (their own gap between the candidates, the turnout decision's interest): people take part more in a survey on a topic that matters to them (Pew Research Center 2017, citing topic salience). Sets the scale of the case; the base, the engagement weight and the trait weight are fitted against it. Fitted on the named voters of three drawn race towns (src/core2/trait-test-kit.ts drawnRaceWorld, 30 days to two days past the race, every module): Finklea, South Carolina (place key 4525405, seed 100a9eddd8c1, 586 voters with a choice), Silver City, Nevada (3266800, 62fd4b12c74d, 122) and Douglas, Nebraska (3113505, d6f5f50c5452, 209).
